book.title: Think and Grow Rich (Düşün ve Zengin Ol)
book.author: Napoleon Hill

confidence_note: The core story is well documented in Chapter 1 ('Thoughts Are Things'): the freight-train arrival, the stated goal of partnership, the low-paid job, the roughly five-year wait and the dictating-machine opportunity. Three details in the existing TR text are not reliably in the book and are left out of the facts. First, the exact year 1905: Hill only says 'more than thirty years ago' or similar. Second, 'hired as a janitor': the book says he got a job in Edison's office at a nominal wage doing unimportant work. Third, staff laughing at him: this does not appear in the book. The arrival place is given as (West) Orange, New Jersey.
facts: Edwin C. Barnes had a burning desire to become a business associate (partner) of Thomas A. Edison, not merely to work for him.
He had no personal acquaintance with Edison and not enough money to pay his railroad fare.
He travelled to Edison's laboratory in (West) Orange, New Jersey, arriving on a freight train.
He presented himself to Edison and said plainly that he had come to go into business with him.
Edison later recalled that Barnes looked like an ordinary tramp. Yet something in his expression showed he was determined to get what he had come for.
Barnes did not get a partnership at that first meeting. He got a job in Edison's offices at a very nominal wage.
For about five years he did work unrelated to his goal. Outwardly nothing seemed to change, but he kept his desire alive.
Edison invented a dictating machine (later sold as the Ediphone), and his salesmen had little enthusiasm for it. Barnes said he could sell it.
He was given the chance and sold it so successfully that Edison gave him a contract to distribute and market the machine nationwide. This became the business association he had wanted.
Hill uses the story to show that a definite purpose, backed by a decision that leaves no route of retreat ('burning bridges'), can turn a thought into a reality.
tension: A man with no money, no connections and no credentials announces he will be partner to the most famous inventor alive, then spends years in a minor job where nothing seems to happen.
opening_idea: Open on the image of a man climbing off a freight car, penniless, about to tell Thomas Edison he has come to be his partner.

lessons.idea: A definite, specific desire is the real starting capital. Resources come after the decision, not before it.
lessons.anchor: Barnes had no fare money and no introduction, only an exact goal: to be Edison's associate.

lessons.idea: Take the entry that is available, even if it looks far from the goal, and keep the goal in view while you do it.
lessons.anchor: He accepted a low-paid office job without dropping the partnership aim.

lessons.idea: Persistence through years of invisible progress is what lets you recognise the opportunity when it arrives, often in a form nobody else wants.
lessons.anchor: The dictating machine that Edison's salesmen doubted became Barnes's breakthrough.

lessons.idea: Removing your own escape routes makes commitment visible to others.
lessons.anchor: Edison read the determination in Barnes's face before Barnes had proven anything.

reflect: Which goal have you shelved because you are waiting to have 'enough' resources first?
Is there an unglamorous position near your goal that you could step into now?
What opportunity around you are others dismissing that you could volunteer for?
reflect_final: If you stated your goal as plainly as Barnes did, what would be your freight-train first step this week?

use_cases.situation: A new product or project at work that colleagues are unenthusiastic about.
use_cases.move: Say in the meeting: 'I'll take this one and bring results in 30 days.' Volunteering for the neglected opportunity is how Barnes got his chance.

use_cases.situation: Talking with a manager or mentor about a role you want but don't yet qualify for.
use_cases.move: State the destination explicitly ('In two years I want to lead X'), then ask which current task would let you prove it.

use_cases.situation: Feeling stuck in a job that seems unrelated to your real ambition.
use_cases.move: Write your specific goal on a card. Each week, list one thing from the current job that moves you toward it or brings you closer to the people who matter.

pocket_idea: Barnes arrived with no money and no connections, only a decision. Five years later that decision made him Edison's partner.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: He arrived by freight car and left with a nationwide Edison contract. The ticket was a decision, not money.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: A penniless man tells Edison he'll be his partner, gets a low-paid office job instead, waits about five years, then offers to sell the dictating machine nobody else believes in, and wins the partnership.
conversation_variants.question_idea: Would you take a minor job next to your goal and keep believing for five years with no visible progress?
conversation_variants.key_contrast_idea: Most people wait for resources before committing. Barnes committed first and let the resources follow.
